title: Isaiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 39 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 39.

questions.question: In Isaiah 39, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Merodachbaladan sent letters and a present to Hezekiah
Hezekiah showed the Babylonians his treasures
Isaiah asked Hezekiah about the men who came to him
Hezekiah said the men came from Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Merodachbaladan sent letters and a present to Hezekiah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:1 describes Merodachbaladan sending letters and a present to Hezekiah as the first event in the chapter.

questions.question: Who sent letters and a present to Hezekiah?
options: Merodachbaladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Merodachbaladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:1 clearly states that Merodachbaladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah.

questions.question: Why did Merodachbaladan send letters and a present to Hezekiah?
options: Because he had heard Hezekiah had been sick and was recovered
Because he wanted to buy spices
Because he wanted to congratulate Hezekiah on a victory
questions.correctAnswer: Because he had heard Hezekiah had been sick and was recovered
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:1 says Merodachbaladan sent gifts because he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick and was recovered.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah feel about the men from Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: He was glad of them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:2 states that Hezekiah was glad of the men from Babylon.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah show the men from Babylon?
options: His house of precious things including silver, gold, spices, ointment, armor, and treasures
questions.correctAnswer: His house of precious things including silver, gold, spices, ointment, armor, and treasures
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:2 lists what Hezekiah showed them: his house of precious things such as silver, gold, spices, ointment, armor, and treasures.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 39:2, was there anything in Hezekiah's house or dominion that he did not show the men?
options: There was nothing he did not show
He hid some of his treasures
He only showed them the gold
He only showed them his armor
questions.correctAnswer: There was nothing he did not show
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:2 states that Hezekiah showed them all that was found in his treasures and nothing was hidden.

questions.question: Who came to Hezekiah after he showed the men from Babylon his treasures?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah the prophet
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:3 says that then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah.

questions.question: What question did Isaiah ask Hezekiah about the men?
options: What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee?
Why did you show them your treasures?
Are you making an alliance with them?
questions.correctAnswer: What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:3 quotes Isaiah asking Hezekiah what the men said and from where they came.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah respond about where the men came from?
options: They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:3 records Hezekiah saying the men came from a far country, Babylon.

questions.question: What items did Hezekiah show that were found in his house?
options: Silver, gold, spices, precious ointment, armour, and treasures
questions.correctAnswer: Silver, gold, spices, precious ointment, armour, and treasures
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:2 lists these items as the precious things Hezekiah showed the men.

questions.question: Who was king of Babylon when the men came to Hezekiah?
questions.correctAnswer: Merodachbaladan, the son of Baladan
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:1 identifies Merodachbaladan, son of Baladan, as king of Babylon at that time.

questions.question: Hezekiah showed the men from Babylon all his treasures and armour.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:2 explicitly states Hezekiah showed the men all his treasures and armour.

questions.question: Isaiah the prophet asked Hezekiah about the origin and message of the men who visited him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:3 records Isaiah asking Hezekiah what the men said and from where they came.

questions.question: The text says Hezekiah sent a gift to Merodachbaladan.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:1 only mentions Merodachbaladan sending letters and a present to Hezekiah, not the other way around.

questions.question: The men from Babylon came to Hezekiah because he was planning a war.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:1 states the men came because they heard Hezekiah had been sick and recovered, not for war.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 39 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah show to the men from Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: His house of precious things
questions.explanation: Hezekiah showed them all that was in his house, including his precious things, as stated in Isaiah 39:2.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 39:6 promise will happen if someone does what Isaiah 39:5 commands?
options: They will be blessed with riches
Their treasures will be taken away
questions.correctAnswer: Their treasures will be taken away
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:6 indicates that if the word of the LORD is not heeded, all that is in the house will be carried to Babylon.

questions.question: What was Hezekiah's response to Isaiah's inquiry about the visitors?
options: He told them everything he had
questions.correctAnswer: He told them everything he had
questions.explanation: Hezekiah answered that all that was in his house had been seen by the Babylonian visitors, as noted in Isaiah 39:4.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 39:6 warn will happen to Hezekiah's treasures?
options: They will be carried to Babylon
They will be shared with the needy
questions.correctAnswer: They will be carried to Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:6 warns that all that is in Hezekiah's house and what his fathers have laid up will be carried away to Babylon.

questions.question: Why was Hezekiah glad when he received visitors from Babylon?
options: He wanted to boast about his wealth
questions.correctAnswer: He was recovering from illness
questions.explanation: Hezekiah was glad of the visitors because they had heard that he was sick and had recovered, as stated in Isaiah 39:1.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned about pride from Hezekiah's actions?
questions.correctAnswer: Pride can lead to downfall
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's pride in showing all his treasures ultimately led to the warning from Isaiah about their loss, indicating that pride can have serious consequences.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah demonstrate integrity in his response to Isaiah?
options: By being honest about what he showed
questions.correctAnswer: By being honest about what he showed
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's response shows integrity as he truthfully stated that he had shown everything in his house, as noted in Isaiah 39:4.

questions.question: What can Christians learn about transparency from Hezekiah's situation?
options: Transparency is a sign of weakness
questions.correctAnswer: Transparency can lead to vulnerability
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's openness about his treasures made him vulnerable to future loss, which illustrates that transparency can have both positive and negative outcomes.

questions.question: In what way does Isaiah 39:5 serve as a warning for future generations?
options: To heed the word of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To heed the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:5 emphasizes the importance of listening to the word of the LORD, serving as a warning for future generations to remain obedient.

questions.question: What attitude should Christians adopt regarding their possessions based on Isaiah 39?
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity and stewardship
questions.explanation: Christians can learn that their possessions are temporary and should be viewed with a mindset of stewardship and generosity, reflecting the message of Isaiah 39.

questions.question: What should be a Christian's response to warnings about pride and materialism?
questions.correctAnswer: Reflect and seek change
questions.explanation: Christians are encouraged to reflect on the warnings about pride and materialism, seeking change to align with God’s desires.

questions.question: What can be inferred about Hezekiah's future based on Isaiah's prophecy?
options: He will lead Israel to victory
questions.correctAnswer: He will face loss
questions.explanation: Isaiah's prophecy in Isaiah 39:6 indicates that Hezekiah's treasures will be carried away, implying a future of loss.

questions.question: Is it important for Christians to be cautious about what they share with others?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: It is true, as Hezekiah's openness led to significant consequences, teaching the importance of discretion in what is shared.

questions.question: Hezekiah believed that showing his treasures would bring glory to God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: It is false; Hezekiah's actions were rooted in pride, not necessarily in bringing glory to God, as evidenced by the consequences he faced.

questions.question: Isaiah indicated that all treasures would be preserved for future generations.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: It is false; Isaiah prophesied that all treasures would be taken away, indicating a loss rather than preservation.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 39.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 39:7, what will happen to the sons of Hezekiah?
options: They shall be taken away and become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon
They shall reign as kings in Jerusalem
They shall be priests in the temple
They shall flee to Egypt for safety
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be taken away and become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:7 clearly states that Hezekiah's sons will be taken away and become eunuchs in the Babylonian king's palace.

questions.question: How does Hezekiah respond to Isaiah's prophecy in Isaiah 39:8?
options: He says the word of the LORD is good and expects peace and truth in his days
He becomes angry and rejects the prophecy
He prays for the destruction of Babylon
He decides to hide his treasures
questions.correctAnswer: He says the word of the LORD is good and expects peace and truth in his days
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:8 records Hezekiah's acceptance of the prophecy and his optimistic view that there will be peace and truth during his lifetime.

questions.question: What is the significance of the word 'eunuchs' in Isaiah 39:7 in the cultural context of Babylon?
options: Eunuchs held significant administrative roles and were often trusted servants
Eunuchs were considered outcasts with no power
Eunuchs were religious leaders in Babylon
Eunuchs were soldiers in the Babylonian army
questions.correctAnswer: Eunuchs held significant administrative roles and were often trusted servants
questions.explanation: The term 'eunuchs' in Isaiah 39:7 refers to castrated males often employed in high-ranking administrative roles within royal courts, including Babylon.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 39:6-7 regarding the fate of Hezekiah's house?
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic warning and foreshadowing
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:6-7 uses prophetic warning and foreshadowing to predict the exile and captivity of Hezekiah's descendants and treasures.

questions.question: In Isaiah 39:8, what two qualities does Hezekiah mention that will characterize his days?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace and truth
questions.explanation: Hezekiah states in Isaiah 39:8 that there will be peace and truth during his lifetime.

questions.question: In Isaiah 39:7, the Hebrew word translated as 'take away' (לקח) implies what kind of action?
options: To forcibly remove or carry off
questions.correctAnswer: To forcibly remove or carry off
questions.explanation: The Hebrew verb לקח (laqach) used in Isaiah 39:7 commonly means 'to take' or 'to carry off,' implying a forceful removal.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'shalom' in Isaiah 39:8 best translate to in English?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'shalom' (שָׁלוֹם) in Isaiah 39:8 means 'peace,' indicating a state of completeness and tranquility.

questions.question: Which literary technique is evident when Isaiah 39:6-7 depicts the removal of treasures and sons to Babylon as a symbol of future exile?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: The passage uses typology by presenting the removal of treasures and sons as a foreshadowing of the Babylonian exile, a key event in Israel’s history.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of prophetic warning about captivity found in Isaiah 39:6-7?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 21:24
questions.explanation: Luke 21:24 references the discipleship and exile of Jerusalem’s people, echoing the captivity theme in Isaiah 39:6-7.

questions.question: Which Old Testament chapter also discusses the fate of Judah's kings' descendants in captivity, similar to Isaiah 39:7?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Kings 24
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24 describes the Babylonian exile and the captivity of Judah’s kings’ descendants, paralleling Isaiah 39:7.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Isaiah's prophecy about the sons becoming eunuchs in Isaiah 39:7?
options: The declaration that all treasures in Hezekiah's house will be carried to Babylon
Hezekiah showing his treasures to the Babylonian envoys
The sending of letters from Merodachbaladan
questions.correctAnswer: The declaration that all treasures in Hezekiah's house will be carried to Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:6 precedes verse 7 and prophesies that all treasures will be taken to Babylon.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 39:2 serve as a literary foreshadowing within the chapter?
options: By Hezekiah showing all his treasures, it foreshadows their eventual seizure by Babylon
It foreshadows a coming war with Babylon
It foreshadows a new temple being built
questions.correctAnswer: By Hezekiah showing all his treasures, it foreshadows their eventual seizure by Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:2 shows Hezekiah proudly displaying his treasures, which foreshadows the prophecy in verses 6-7 that these treasures will be taken away.

questions.question: The phrase 'peace and truth' in Isaiah 39:8 can be understood to parallel which Hebrew literary concept?
questions.correctAnswer: Emet and Shalom
questions.explanation: The words 'truth' and 'peace' in Hebrew correspond to 'Emet' (truth) and 'Shalom' (peace), representing completeness and faithfulness as in Isaiah 39:8.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 39:8, Hezekiah accepted the prophecy about his descendants' fate with a positive attitude, expecting peace in his own days.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:8 shows Hezekiah saying, 'Good is the word of the LORD' and expecting peace and truth in his days, indicating acceptance and optimism.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 39:6 states that some treasures of Hezekiah's house will remain in Jerusalem and not be taken to Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:6 explicitly states that 'nothing shall be left' but all treasures will be carried to Babylon.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 39 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 39:6 teach about God's sovereignty in relation to human history and the fate of nations?
options: God sovereignly ordains the exile of Judah's treasures to Babylon as part of His redemptive plan
God passively allows Babylon to take treasures due to human free will
God is unaware of future events concerning Judah's treasures
God promises to protect Judah's treasures from all foreign powers
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains the exile of Judah's treasures to Babylon as part of His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:6 states 'Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house... shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the LORD.' This shows God's sovereign control over the exile, not a passive allowance or ignorance.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and its consequences is demonstrated in Isaiah 39:7?
options: Sin leads to the captivity and humiliation of God's people, including the removal of royal offspring
Sin has no effect on the lineage of kings
God will immediately forgive and restore without consequences
Human sin is irrelevant to political exile
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to the captivity and humiliation of God's people, including the removal of royal offspring
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:7 predicts that Hezekiah's descendants will be taken captive and made eunuchs in Babylon, illustrating consequences of sin affecting even the king's family.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's prophetic revelation is taught in Isaiah 39:5?
options: God communicates future judgment through His prophets to warn His people
Prophets only speak of present events without future insight
God hides future events from His prophets
Prophetic messages are optional and do not require heeding
questions.correctAnswer: God communicates future judgment through His prophets to warn His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:5 says 'Hear the word of the LORD of hosts,' showing that God uses prophets to reveal forthcoming judgment to His people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 39:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 39:5, God reveals future events through Isaiah the prophet, demonstrating His attribute of divine revelation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 39:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:6 shows God exercising sovereign control over nations and history by declaring the exile of Judah's treasures to Babylon.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 39 contribute to the broader biblical theme of covenant judgment and restoration?
options: It foreshadows the Babylonian exile as a covenantal consequence, preparing for eventual restoration
It denies any covenant relationship between God and His people
It focuses solely on political alliances without divine involvement
It promises immediate restoration without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the Babylonian exile as a covenantal consequence, preparing for eventual restoration
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39's prophecy about exile anticipates covenant judgment, linking with themes in Deuteronomy and later restoration promises in Isaiah 40–66.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Isaiah 39 have with the New Testament theme of suffering and exile?
options: It prefigures the spiritual exile and suffering believers face, pointing to ultimate deliverance in Christ
It contradicts New Testament teachings on suffering
It exclusively applies to ancient Israel without typological significance
It teaches that exile is purely political without spiritual meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the spiritual exile and suffering believers face, pointing to ultimate deliverance in Christ
questions.explanation: The exile in Isaiah 39 typifies the believer’s spiritual exile, which the New Testament addresses through Christ’s redemption (Hebrews 11:13-16).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Isaiah 39:2 and Isaiah 39:4 teach about human pride and divine judgment?
options: Human pride in worldly treasures provokes divine judgment and loss
Displaying wealth ensures divine favor and protection
God ignores human pride and materialism
Human pride is unrelated to divine plans
questions.correctAnswer: Human pride in worldly treasures provokes divine judgment and loss
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's showing of treasures (39:2,4) reveals pride, which precedes Isaiah's judgment announcement (39:6), linking pride with coming judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 39:7 and Isaiah 39:8 teach about human response to divine prophecy?
options: Humans often misunderstand or minimize divine judgment as peaceful
Humans always repent fully upon hearing prophecy
Prophecy is universally rejected and ignored
questions.correctAnswer: Humans often misunderstand or minimize divine judgment as peaceful
questions.explanation: Hezekiah calls the harsh judgment in 39:7 'good' and 'peace' in 39:8, showing a misunderstanding or minimization of God's warning.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 39:1 and Isaiah 39:3 teach about God's providence and human political relations?
options: God's providence governs international events including sickness and diplomatic contact
Politics operate independently of God's providence
God causes political alliances to fail
Sickness is unrelated to divine providence
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence governs international events including sickness and diplomatic contact
questions.explanation: The news of Hezekiah's sickness and recovery (39:1) prompts Babylonian envoys (39:3), illustrating God's providential orchestration of political and personal events.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Isaiah 39:6-7 teaches that God arbitrarily punishes Israel without cause. What does Isaiah 39:5-8 actually teach?
options: God's judgment is righteous and follows human actions, with Hezekiah's response showing misunderstanding of God's plans
God randomly punishes without warning or reason
God's judgment is unjust and arbitrary
God promises no judgment and only blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is righteous and follows human actions, with Hezekiah's response showing misunderstanding of God's plans
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:5-8 reveals God's sober warning of exile due to covenant unfaithfulness, with Hezekiah mistakenly embracing peace despite judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 39:1 teach about God's providence in relation to human sickness and recovery?
options: God's providence governs personal health events, which have wider political implications
God is indifferent to human sickness
Sickness and recovery are only natural events without divine involvement
Recovery is always a sign of divine approval
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence governs personal health events, which have wider political implications
questions.explanation: Merodachbaladan's sending gifts after Hezekiah's recovery (39:1) shows that God’s providence over sickness affects international relations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 39:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:7 predicts the exile and eunuch-ization of Hezekiah's descendants as a just consequence for covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Isaiah 39:8 have with the theme of false peace in biblical theology?
options: Hezekiah's declaration of peace despite impending judgment illustrates the danger of false security apart from God
It affirms that all peace is from God and always genuine
It denies any future judgment or exile
It shows that peace is unrelated to covenant obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah's declaration of peace despite impending judgment illustrates the danger of false security apart from God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 39:8 reveals Hezekiah's complacency and false peace, a common biblical theme warning against ignoring divine judgment (cf. Jeremiah 6:14).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 39:2 and Isaiah 39:6 teach about human trust in material wealth versus divine sovereignty?
options: Human trust in material wealth is futile because God's sovereignty can remove all earthly treasures
Material wealth guarantees divine favor and security
God ignores human wealth in His plans
Earthly treasures are inviolable by divine will
questions.correctAnswer: Human trust in material wealth is futile because God's sovereignty can remove all earthly treasures
questions.explanation: Hezekiah proudly shows his riches (39:2), yet God declares all will be carried to Babylon (39:6), highlighting trust in wealth as ultimately futile.
